summary: Tested enhancements to Compare Sales Daywise (/compare-sales-daywise, admin). PASSED: Cumulative column renders by default (sub-th count 4 per year); cumulative math is exact (per-row running sum of Sales, '—' carries forward); cum@countdown=2 (date 10/02) = 494.816 = sum of 02/02..10/02 sales; final cum@countdown=0 = 622.454 = Total row figure. Main-page cum-toggle hides/shows Cum. column (4↔3 sub-cols). Print preview toolbar shows toolbar-cum-toggle and view-pdf-btn; toolbar toggle updates preview table live. view-pdf-btn opens a blob: URL (window.open captured) with content-type application/pdf (size 12710 bytes) — no console errors during PDF generation. Regression: font +/- (10→11→10), spacing +/- (4→5→4), orientation toggle, Clear wipes table + LS — all pass. FAILED (1 bug): showCum toggle state is NOT persisted across reload. Verified by LS inspection: before reload LS has {showCum:false}, after reload LS is overwritten to {showCum:true} and UI reverts to Cum column ON.

ui_bugs.issue: Toggling Cumulative OFF on the main page writes showCum:false to localStorage correctly, but after a page reload the save-useEffect fires on mount with stale closure (initial showCum=true) and immediately OVERWRITES the loaded value back to true. Result: toggle state does not survive reload; table always rebuilds with Cum. column ON. RCA: in CompareSalesDaywise.jsx, the load useEffect (lines 44-60) sets loadedRef.current=true BEFORE the save useEffect's (lines 62-69) first run in the same commit. The save effect's guard `if (!loadedRef.current) return;` therefore passes, but its closure still has the initial render values (showCum=true), so it writes true to LS before the setShowCum(false) is reflected in a subsequent render. Fix: either (a) flip loadedRef via a separate `useEffect(() => { loadedRef.current = true; }, [])` placed AFTER both effects, (b) replace loadedRef with a state var `loaded` and guard the save effect with it (so save re-runs only after a render where loaded===true), or (c) explicitly set LS inside the load effect once and skip the first fire of the save effect using a skip counter. Toolbar (preview) toggle works live; the bug is only persistence.

action_items: Fix showCum persistence race in /app/frontend/src/pages/CompareSalesDaywise.jsx — the save useEffect for print prefs runs on mount with stale default state (showCum=true) and clobbers the just-loaded value in localStorage. Recommended fix: convert loadedRef to a `loaded` state variable (default false), set it to true inside the load useEffect, and guard the save useEffect with `if (!loaded) return;`. This ensures the save effect only fires on renders AFTER the load completed, with correct closure values.
critical_code_review_comments: The two useEffects in CompareSalesDaywise.jsx share state via a useRef guard that is set in the SAME commit as the save effect runs — classic stale-closure/same-tick ordering bug. Use state (not ref) for 'has loaded' gating when the gated effect depends on loaded values.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All iter-54 enhancements verified except cum-toggle persistence across reload (HIGH bug — see RCA). Known seed data: 2026-02-12 anchor with daysBack=10 produces sales [54.277,73.889,44.248,57.789,35.696,64.461,—,70.917,93.539,79.141,48.497] and running cums [54.277,128.166,172.414,230.203,265.899,330.360,330.360,401.277,494.816,573.957,622.454]; Total=622.454 kg. 08/02 has no sales (shown as '—') and cum carries forward correctly. New data-testids added in iter-54: cum-toggle (main-page Switch), toolbar-cum-toggle (preview toolbar Switch), view-pdf-btn (preview toolbar). view-pdf-btn opens blob URL via window.open; override window.open to capture.
rca of the issue: File: /app/frontend/src/pages/CompareSalesDaywise.jsx. Mount useEffect (deps=[]) loads saved state including showCum and sets `loadedRef.current = true` at its end. The second useEffect (deps=[fontPt,cellPad,orientation,showCum]) that persists print prefs runs in the SAME commit immediately after, and its closure captures the initial-render state (showCum=true, loadedRef.current now true because effects share the mutable ref), so it writes `showCum:true` to localStorage before the setShowCum(false) scheduled by the load effect causes a re-render. On the next render it writes the correct value, but the user then navigates/reloads believing LS is correct. However when the user has ALREADY toggled to false (LS=false) and reloads, exactly the same race replays: load reads false → calls setShowCum(false) → save effect fires with stale showCum=true and overwrites LS back to true. Reproduction: (1) on /compare-sales-daywise with a built table, toggle cum-toggle OFF (LS correctly becomes showCum:false), (2) reload the page. Expected: Cum. column hidden, LS still false. Actual: Cum. column visible, LS reverted to true. Mitigation: replace loadedRef (useRef) with a `loaded` useState bool; guard the save effect with the state value so it only runs on renders AFTER loaded===true, by which point showCum closure is current.
